### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, all observed outgoing transitions of A17 (58 transitions) led to A40, with no other successor observed. In the later window, about 97 in 100 observed outgoing transitions of A17 still led to A40, while about 1 in 38 (roughly 3 in 100) led to A46, a successor that did not appear in the earlier window [DIR001].
- The absolute size of this routing difference is small (cosine dissimilarity about 0.0004), though it exceeds about 995 of 1,000 random re-splits of the pooled data; the later-window profile rests on only 38 observed transitions, and the new A46 edge on a single transition [DIR001].

### Inference

Support level: Insufficient evidence

The evidence is insufficient to infer a change in the process. Only one item qualified across 92 tested units while about 0.46 items would be expected by chance in an unchanged process — exactly what a stable process typically produces — and the possible new successor edge A17 → A46 rests on roughly 1 of 38 observed outgoing transitions in the later window, so a rare variant cannot be ruled out [DIR001].

- After: A17 → A40 in ~97.4% and A17 → A46 in ~2.6% of observed outgoing transitions (38 observations in after window)
